newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST-New Zealand Business Weeklies-Oct 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-New Zealand Business Weeklies-Oct 4.

text.p: Dover Samuels, the number three candidate on the Labour party list, is embroiled in a bitter court battle to expel him as trustee of Northland's Mahimahi E5 Maori Trust. Page 1.

The battle for control of Power New Zealand reached fever pitch this week with legal action filed against Waipa District Council and Mercury Energy alleging breach of contract by Power NZ. Last week, Waipa District Council announced its sale of Power NZ shares for $10 a share to Mercury Energy. But Power NZ's independent directors' chairman, Barry Brill, lambasted the
sale as "unethical, immoral and illegal". Power NZ was determined to resist the Mercury takeover. Page 1.

The float price of Brierley Investments' biggest asset, Thistle Hotels, was forced down by a rash of hotel floats, hard-nosed British fund managers and expectations BIL would eventually sell out of Thistle. The 170 pence price means BIL would take a loss on the sale of its shares, valued on company books at 181 pence. This would be offset by a special dividend from Thistle, leaving BIL with a small surplus from the deal. Page 3.

Former National Finance Minister Ruth Richardson is telling voters to back ACT NZ with their party vote. Richardson said the country was in danger of voting a left-wing coalition government into power. She also criticised Prime Minister Jim Bolger for his "negative, uninspiring" leadership of the National campaign. Page 4.

Fertiliser company Bay of Plenty Co-operative, extended its offer for SouthFert by 20 days to October 21. The trouble was an earlier offer by Ravensdown accepted by SouthFert shareholders was blocked by the Commerce Commission. Ravensdown's appeal to the High Court will not be heard until October 11. BoP's offer was conditional on the appeal failing. Page 4.

Ron Brierley's Guiness Peat Group is believed to have retained most of the A$17.9 million settlement agreed last week between GPG and Australian oil and gas company Ampolex on their long-standing legal fight over six million Ampolex notes. The
settlement paved the way for Mobil Corp to complete its A$1.8 billion takeover of Ampolex. Page 4.

Television New Zealand faces increasing pressure to slash staff numbers and fixed costs to compete with TV3's new shoestring channel. The state-owned broadcaster has 1,700 staff at its three channels, six times more than TV3. TVNZ had been under increasing pressure this year to meet ambitious Treasury targets to increase profits and dividends to the government. Page 1.

Chief executives remain confident of the future of New Zealand's economy and their companies, despite the National Party government's warning to the contrary, according to the first NBR and Ernst and Young Quarterly CEO Survey. Surveyed in September, many chief executives felt the economy would remain flat for the rest of 1996, but they expected interest rates to continue falling and inflation to decline in 1997. Page 1.

The Serious Fraud Office is investigating the merger of Kiwi and Tui dairy companies after receiving complaints about material sent to shareholders. It was understood to involve an information memorandum circulated by Kiwi directors to suppliers before the merger. It set out the operating scenario for the merged company, with estimated earnings under the anticipated market conditions of the next few years. Page 1.

The fact that Mercury Energy and UtiliCorp's latest bids for Power New Zealand shares are well above any realistic valuation comes as no surprise, but Bancorp's appraisal of the target comapny is a valuable benchmarking tool for assessing the volatile electricity industry. Page 2.
The Internet industry believes a dangerous precedent has been set by the government-driven clampdown on access to newsgroups. Page 3.

The National Party government is adamant it will not be put off highlighting the alleged threat to the economy posed by a centre-left coalition, despite comments by credit rating agency Standard and Poor the election result was unlikely to affect New Zealand's AA+ rating. Page 3.

Forty-six percent of voters believe National would be part of a governing coalition, according to the latest NBR-Consultus poll. Seventy-four percent think National would win the most seats and 62 percent expect Jim Bolger to remain prime minister. And 35 percent tipped New Zealand First to be part of a
coalition government, 27 percent tipped Labour and 19 percent picked the Alliance. Page 14.
